title: Logprobs and confidence signals
summary: Logprobs expose the log probability of each generated token and its top alternatives. They are a usable but uncalibrated signal for classification confidence and abstention.
useIf: You classify with a non-reasoning model and want a threshold to escalate or abstain.
avoidIf: You treat a high token probability as proof that a fact is true, or your model path drops logprobs.

explain.md: With `logprobs` on, the API returns the log probability of each chosen token and, with `top_logprobs` (0 to 20), the most likely alternatives. In Chat Completions set `logprobs: true` and `top_logprobs`. In Responses set `top_logprobs` and add `message.output_text.logprobs` to `include` [[r4]] [[r5]]. A log probability converts to a probability with `exp`, so -0.105 is about 0.90.

explain.title: From logprob to probability

vars.v: Natural-log probability returned for a token, always 0 or negative
Probability of that token given the preceding text

explain.example: A one-token label `refund` with logprob -0.105 has p = exp(-0.105) = 0.90. If the top alternative `cancel` has -2.3, its p is about 0.10.

explain.md: The standard pattern is a **classifier with a single-token label**: ask for one label, set a tiny token cap, read the label's probability, and escalate to a human or a larger model below a threshold. Pick labels whose first tokens differ, or probability splits across variants.

explain.title: Availability depends on the model path
explain.md: OpenAI says that when effort is not `none` you should remove `logprobs` and `top_logprobs`, and remove `message.output_text.logprobs` from `include` [[r2]]. The Azure page marks `logprobs` as supported on the GPT-6 models while its reasoning page lists it as rejected [[r15]]. Anthropic Messages has no `logprobs`, and the OpenAI compatibility layer ignores it [[r36]].

whereToUse: Routing and triage classifiers that must escalate uncertain cases
Cascades: accept the small model's answer only above a probability threshold
Highlighting low-confidence tokens in an extraction review tool
Ranking candidate completions or comparing label options
Monitoring drift: a shift in the average label probability can flag a model or data change

use: The output is a short label from a small set
You can build a labelled set to calibrate thresholds
avoid: Trusting raw probabilities across models or after a model update
Using logprobs on free-form long answers as a truth score
Reasoning paths that drop the parameter
flips: You move to a reasoning model or Claude: use sampled agreement, a verifier or retrieval signals
Labels share first tokens: rename them or compare full-sequence probabilities
The cost of a wrong accept is high: add a second signal before acting

alternatives.title: Choosing a confidence signal
head: Signal
Wins when
Loses when
Cost or risk
rows: Judge shares the generator's blind spots

pitfalls.symptom: A 0.95 probability label is wrong often
pitfalls.cause: Raw token probabilities are not calibrated against accuracy
pitfalls.fix: Plot accuracy by probability bucket on labelled data and set thresholds from that curve

pitfalls.cause: Several labels start with the same token or have variants
pitfalls.fix: Use labels with distinct first tokens or sum variants before comparing

pitfalls.symptom: 400 or missing logprobs after enabling reasoning
pitfalls.fix: Use effort `none` where supported, or switch signals

scenarios.title: Escalating uncertain tickets
scenarios.situation: A non-reasoning model labels support tickets into six queues. Wrong routes waste agent time. The team has 3,000 labelled tickets.
constraints: Escalation to a human is available
unknowns: How accurate is the model at each probability level?
What share of tickets may be escalated?
scenarios.question: How do you decide when to escalate?

options.name: Ask the model for a confidence number in the answer
options.why: Verbal confidence is rarely calibrated, and it costs extra output tokens.
options.tradeoff: It is the fallback when logprobs are unavailable.

options.name: Read the label's logprob and set a threshold from an accuracy-by-probability curve on the labelled set
options.why: It is free, per request and calibrated on your own data, which fits a labelled, single-token task.
options.tradeoff: Recalibrate after model updates, and the signal vanishes on reasoning paths.

options.name: Run five samples and escalate on disagreement
options.why: Works on any model and catches unstable answers.
options.tradeoff: Five times the cost and added latency.

flips.then: Use sampled agreement or a verifier.

flips.if: Volume is tiny and cost is not a concern
flips.then: Sampled agreement is simpler to explain.

scenarios.takeaway: Calibrate a free signal on your labels before you trust it.

scenarios.title: Confidence on a reasoning model
scenarios.situation: A team moved a classifier to a reasoning model at effort `medium` and the request that asks for `logprobs` fails. They still need an escalation signal.
unknowns: Is extra latency acceptable for a second check?
scenarios.question: What is the best path?

options.name: Keep `logprobs` and ignore the error
options.why: The call fails or drops the field when effort is not `none`, so there is no signal.
options.tradeoff: Valid only on a path where the model supports the parameter.

options.name: Use sampled agreement or a lightweight verifier check on low-stakes labels and escalate disagreements
options.why: Works with reasoning models and gives a usable signal.
options.tradeoff: Costs more calls and needs evals.

options.name: Test whether a non-reasoning model at effort `none` keeps accuracy, and use its logprobs if it does
options.why: It restores the free per-request signal if accuracy holds, which an eval can show.
options.tradeoff: If accuracy drops, you need the agreement or verifier path.

flips.then: Keep the reasoning model and add the agreement check.
Add a verifier or human review regardless of the signal.

scenarios.takeaway: Pick the signal your model path supports, then validate it.

quiz.q: A label token has logprob -0.105. What is its probability, to two decimals?
quiz.explain: p = exp(-0.105) = 0.90. Logprobs are natural logs, so exponentiate to get a probability.

quiz.q: Why is a raw token probability a weak stand-alone confidence score?
options: It is not calibrated to accuracy and reflects token likelihood, not truth
quiz.explain: A token can be likely yet wrong. Calibrate thresholds on labelled data. The other options are false.

quiz.q: On which paths should you not expect `logprobs`?
options: OpenAI reasoning calls with effort not `none`
OpenAI Chat Completions on a non-reasoning model
quiz.explain: Anthropic Messages has no logprobs, OpenAI removes them when effort is not `none`, and the compatibility layer ignores them. A non-reasoning Chat call supports them.

flashcards.front: How do you turn a logprob into a probability?
flashcards.back: Apply `exp`. A logprob of -0.105 gives about 0.90.

flashcards.front: What is the single-token label pattern?
flashcards.back: Ask for one label with a tiny token cap, read its probability and escalate below a threshold calibrated on labelled data.

flashcards.front: Why prefer labels with distinct first tokens?
flashcards.back: Probability splits across variants that share a first token, which makes the comparison unreliable.
